limitations: The intervention changes all box shadows together. It does not identify one selector, blur radius, shader implementation or exact browser CPU cause.
All native ISA/runtime/source/actual-controller identities and workload operations are matched; jobs do not establish identical physical hardware or repeat reliability. This is one cohort.

The owned document has a fixed parser-created stylesheet/marker insertion with original source bytes and security headers verified. Original app.js/app.css/API responses are untouched, but this remains a distinct diagnostic harness.

Marker timing proves stylesheet readiness while the body is absent and before application readiness. Global frame callbacks can occur on an empty document and are not actual paint timestamps. Earlier dynamic-loader partial results retain their original failed conditions.
No control cost is subtracted from production metrics; no observed diagnostic timing awards original baseline, sustained or installed acceptance.

Even without any box shadow, the ARM64 WebKit worst editor observation remains above500ms. A production candidate still requires original normal/sustained/native acceptance and cannot be qualified from this group comparison.
Firefox sustained RSS failures, installed/native, signing, eight-hour, managed-deployment and held investigation requirements remain open.
